summary: Olivet is one of the 22 communes of Orléans Métropole, just south of Orléans, and its parking policy is very different from Orléans: the commune says all of its roughly 600 public spaces are free, with 430 in the town centre, and it controls turnover with red (20 minutes), blue (1h30, parking disc) and white (no limit) zones instead of paid meters. A 2017 study found the town-centre supply well sized, with peaks on market days, Saturday late morning and school exit times, and the commune said it would optimise rather than add centre car parks. The two sites in the live feed, Victor Hugo (141 spaces) and Les Aulnaies (244), are park-and-rides on tram line A, listed in the Métropole open data with Effia as manager. The Métropole's published policy is to cut solo driving and encourage tram and bus use. The main development in the centre is the Éclosion housing project (about 300 homes), where a December 2024 plan proposed a 40-space landscaped blue-zone car park on rue Paul Genain. No resident-permit scheme, paid zone or EV charging policy specific to Olivet was found; two Métropole-owned charging stations exist.

items.text: The commune's page (read on 21 October 2026) says Olivet has over 600 parking spaces, 430 of them in the town centre, and that all parking is free but time-limited. It describes three zones: red (20 minutes), blue (1h30 with a parking disc) and white (no time limit, abusive parking sanctioned after seven days).

The same page (read on 21 October 2026) names 11 town-centre car parks: Mairie, T. Jourdan, La Petite Borde, Marcel Belot, Jules-Marie Simon, Louis Sallé, Marie Curie, Ronsard, Arcades, Savonniers and Marronniers. The page names no operator and describes parking as free.

In June 2017 the commune reported a study by the firm IPROCIA based on vehicle counts in the centre car parks (weekdays including the Friday market, and Saturday morning). It found the supply well sized, with saturation peaks on market day, Saturday late morning and at school exit times, and every centre car park within 5 minutes' walk of the shops. This is a 2017 finding and may no longer hold.
items.source_title: Le magazine d'Olivet n°185, June 2017 (dossier on parking)

items.text: In the same 2017 magazine the commune said it did not plan new car parks in the centre but would optimise existing ones with better signage and adjusted blue, white and red bays, and that parking would stay free everywhere. It also stated that the 345 homes planned in the Clos du Bourg would have on average two underground spaces each. At that time the fine for overstaying a blue or red bay was 17 euros, as the magazine states.
items.source_title: Le magazine d'Olivet n°185, June 2017 (dossier on parking)

items.text: The Orléans Métropole open-data export read on 21 October 2026 lists two Olivet park-and-rides on tram line A, Victor Hugo (141 spaces, 3 accessible, boulevard Victor Hugo) and Les Aulnaies (244 spaces, 5 accessible, rue de la Bergeresse). Both have Effia stationnement as manager and are flagged with real-time availability. The third Olivet-area site, Zénith (190 spaces), is listed in the feed under the Orléans commune code, not Olivet's.
items.source_title: Parcs de stationnement - Orléans Métropole (open data export)

items.text: Olivet's page (read on 21 October 2026) says three park-and-rides in Olivet serve tram line A (Zénith / Parc des Expositions, Victor Hugo, Les Aulnaies). A Tao ticket validated on arrival gives access, and the P+R ticket gives unlimited parking plus a return fare for everyone in the car, up to 7 people.

The Métropole's 2024 key-figures report describes park-and-rides as free, secure car parks reserved for public-transport users, with 12 tram P+R along the two tram lines and 4 bus P+R. A chart gives yearly P+R attendance for 2018-2023, but its labels could not be read reliably from the text, so no figure is quoted here.
items.source_title: Les chiffres clés de la mobilité dans la métropole orléanaise 2024

items.text: The Métropole's parking page (read on 21 October 2026) sets the aim of reducing solo car driving in favour of tram, bus and active modes, and of encouraging long stays in car parks and short stays on street. Its paid on-street zones, 15-minute free orange-zone rule and 25-euro post-parking charge are described for Orléans and Fleury-les-Aubrais, not for Olivet, where the commune says parking is free.

The Métropole's mobility page (read on 21 October 2026) lists the Urban Mobility Plan (PDU) 2019-2028. The 2024 key-figures report says it was adopted in July 2019, expires in 2028 and will be replaced by a first Mobility Plan (PDM) in 2028, with a mid-term review starting in the second half of 2024.

On Olivet's bus and tram page (read on 21 October 2026), tram line A is 18 km with 24 stations and runs every 5.5 minutes at peak and every 7 minutes off-peak. Bus lines 1 (to La Source hospital), 13 (town hall, Victor Hugo tram stop, university), 17, 22 and 23 serve Olivet, and a night on-demand service, Résa'NUIT, has covered all 22 communes since 1 September 2025.
items.source_title: En bus et en tram (Ville d'Olivet)

items.text: The Métropole's EV-charging open data lists two Olivet stations, rue de l'Yvette and 238 rue du Général de Gaulle, each with 2 points of 22 kW on street, paid, open 24/7 and put into service on 15 July 2021. The dataset was last modified in July 2023, so the list may be incomplete or outdated.
items.source_title: Infrastructures de recharge pour véhicules électriques - Orléans Métropole (open data)

items.text: The Métropole's page says that from 1 January 2024 its charge points cost 0.50 euro per kWh including tax from the first minute, with a 25-euro flat fee to deter long stays. The Olivet stations are listed with Orléans Métropole as developer, so this tariff presumably applies, but the page does not name them. The same page counts 30 Métropole stations across the 22 communes.
According to the Métropole's 2024 key-figures report, the metropolis had 287 public-access EV charge points in 2023 (251 normal, 36 fast), 54% of those in the Loiret department.
items.source_title: Les chiffres clés de la mobilité dans la métropole orléanaise 2024

items.text: At a public meeting on 12 December 2024 on the Éclosion (ex-Clos du Bourg) town-centre project, the commune and the developer SEMDO presented a landscaped car park on rue Paul Genain with 40 blue-zone spaces. Estimated works cost 500,000 euros excluding VAT, with works planned April to August 2025 and opening September-October 2025. This was a proposal; the opening was not confirmed in the sources found.
items.source_title: ZAC du Clos du Bourg - réunion publique 12 décembre 2024 (presentation)

items.text: The commune's Éclosion page (read on 21 October 2026) describes about 300 homes and a pedestrian mall between place Louis Sallé and the Poutyl park, with a financial contribution from the commune of 18.3 million euros. A cafe-restaurant is due to open at the end of 2027 or early 2028, and the page mentions a landscaped car park among the December 2024 changes.

On 17 October 2024 the Métropole council chose Keolis to run the TAO mobility services for 6 years from 1 January 2025; the press release lists park-and-rides (P+R) among the services in the contract. It also sets a target of 20% more network ridership by 2030 (35.6 million trips in 2023). The open-data feed still names Effia stationnement as manager of the Olivet P+R sites, which this release does not explain.
items.source_title: Une nouvelle DSP pour un service simplifié et accessible à tous les habitants (press release, Orléans Métropole)
